quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol is consumed
How often the drinker consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the drinker consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and the drinker's body weight. Driving under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: You should maintain a minimum following distance of two seconds. In bad weather or poor conditions, increase this to at least three seconds.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, you should:

options.text: Move to the right part of the lane so they see you in their side mirror.
Move to the left part of the lane to see better ahead.
Stay in the center part of the lane so they see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the left part of the lane to see better ahead.
questions.explanation: Move to the left part of your lane when passing. This helps you see ahead better and makes you more visible to other drivers. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up and leave it behind.
questions.explanation: Downshift and slow down as the dog approaches. Then speed up and leave it behind. If a larger animal is chasing you, brake and get ready to stop.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Follow the headlights of the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the headlights of the vehicle ahead of you.
questions.explanation: To stay safe at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead of you to see farther down the road. Change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane.
Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane so other drivers see you.
Weave back and forth so drivers notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position to always use. Change your position as road and traffic conditions require.

questions.question: When following a car, the best part of the lane to ride in is usually:
questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane behind a car. This makes you visible in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip from car drippings. This strip:

options.text: Is usually safe for motorcyclists unless the road is wet.
Improves traction for most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe for motorcyclists unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil drippings collect in the center of traffic lanes. On dry roads, this strip usually has enough traction for motorcycles. On wet roads, avoid it. The strip is usually narrow enough that you can ride around it while still staying in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: Goggles, a face shield, or a windshield:

options.text: Must be used when riding faster than 35 mph.
Must be used at all times.
Are required only for riders under 21.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be used when riding faster than 35 mph.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle has no windshield, you must wear shatterproof goggles, glasses, or a face shield when riding above 35 mph. This protects your eyes from wind, debris, and other materials on the road.

questions.question: When riding in a group, you should:

options.text: Place new riders at the back of the group.
Maintain proper spacing and not tailgate other riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain proper spacing and not tailgate other riders.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation when riding in a group. Check your mirrors to watch other riders. Experienced riders should lead and ride at the back. Always keep proper spacing between riders.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you from behind, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases the chance of a collision. Riding on the far side may make the other driver return to your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: What does it mean when an operator's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward?

options.text: The operator plans to turn left.
The operator is about to stop.
The operator plans to turn right.
The operator is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The operator plans to turn right.
questions.explanation: Operators use hand signals to show turns or stops when they do not have mechanical turn signals. When an operator's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, the operator is signaling a right turn or lane change to the right.

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Allow you to set up for turns.
Help you avoid wind from other vehicles.
Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind from other vehicles, stay out of blind spots, and avoid road hazards. Your lane position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right turn
questions.explanation: Operators use hand signals to show turns or stops. When an operator's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, the operator is signaling a right turn or lane change to the right.

questions.question: When riding with a heavy load, what should you adjust?
questions.correctAnswerText: The suspension.
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to the settings recommended for that weight.

questions.question: If road conditions require longer stopping distance, what should you do?

options.text: Ask someone else to ride your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: You need a longer following distance when your motorcycle will take longer to stop. If the pavement is slippery, you cannot see ahead, or traffic is heavy, increase your distance to at least three seconds.

questions.question: What following distance should you normally maintain?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of the lane when preparing to pass on the left. This gives you a better view and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: How do you regain control if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Accelerate while keeping the brake engaged.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Release the rear brake to regain control of a locked rear wheel. However, if you lock the rear brake on good pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: When carrying a load in a sidecar, how does it affect stopping distance?

options.text: It stays the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may increase.
questions.explanation: Adding a load increases the motorcycle's weight and inertia, which may increase stopping distance. Start slowing and stopping earlier when riding a motorcycle with a load or passenger in a sidecar.
